description: Solo team working on Challenge1 : The Interplanetary Museum on the Moon/Mars. I am a Risk Controller focusing on sustainable space heritage protection, autonomous AI dome construction, circular upcycling of orbital debris, and connecting humanity through live 3D/VR experiences.
summary: I developed The Interplanetary Museum on the Moon/Mars, an autonomous, sustainable museum concept designed to protect historical landing sites (such as the Apollo 11 Eagle lander, Opportunity, and Curiosity) in-situ. Leaving historic rovers unprotected exposes priceless human heritage to razor-sharp lunar dust, cosmic radiation, and micro-meteorites, while returning them to Earth is prohibitively expensive. My solution uses AI-guided robots with LiDAR ''No-Go Zone'' and electromagnetic dust plates to safely clean the site, inflate a Kevlar inner dome, and 3D-print a thick protective shell of melted local regolith. Non-historical debris (titanium, aluminum, solar panels, LED lights, and displays) is upcycled to power and build the Hall of Honor. Protected by silica-glass windows and Mars storm shutters, the museum serves as a place of mental rest for astonauts and streams live 3D/VR tours to everyone on Earth-preserving our past while creating a clean, inclusive fresh start in space.
details:
The Interplanetary Museum turns historic off-world landing sites into interactive, protected galleries that remain open to both astronauts in space and virtual visitors on Earth. To make this vision safe en realistic in deep space, I approached the engineering through a risk-managemant lens, accounting for extreme day-and-night temperature swings, cosmic radiation, micro-meteorites, and the 24 -minute communication delay between Earth and Mars. By introducting autonomous LiDAR ''No-Go Zone'', self-repairing regolith bots, and electrostatic airlocks, the facility operates safely without human intervention or damage to fragile artifacts.

Sustainability and long-term maintenance were equally central to my design. Rather than relying on expensive cargo launches from Earth, the museum achieves complete circularity by repurposing existing orbital hardware and running on recycled solar and battery grids during harsh lunar nights.

I created the 7-slide architectural presentation using Microsoft PowerPoint and shared it via Google Drive. Ultimately, the project is designed to bridge the gap between industrial space exploration and human culture-creating a lasting sanctuary for astronauts and an accessible, live 3D/VR window into space for people everywhere.
